records.name: Anderss
records.facts_used: Anderss: The name belongs to the Andreas/Andrejs family, based on Greek andreios, manly, from anēr, man. The family spread in Europe through Christian tradition. Its forms were shortened and adapted differently across languages, so a shared family does not imply identical spelling histories. The Latvian Language Agency gives the exact rendering Anders → Anderss, citing page 99 of a 2003 manual. This dated record illustrates transmission between languages; it is not a first birth registration or proof of one borrowing route in every family.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact given-name rendering checked; no universal borrowing route or first birth registration inferred. Hungarian András is distinguished from Faroese Andras; Ukrainian Andrijs from long-ā or missing-j forms.
